bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ in lwan's fuzz-only config reader helper. The staged `poc` file is 32770 bytes, but `config_fuzzer.cc` truncates it to the first 32768 bytes to fill `static_data[32768]`; that copied prefix ends with byte `0x24` (`'$'`). `config_open_for_fuzzing()` then initializes the lexer on the full 32768-byte buffer, so `config_init_data()` sets `lexer.end` to `static_data + 32768`, the first byte past the global array. When `lex_config()` reads that final `$`, its `$`-lookahead calls `peek()` with `lexer.pos == lexer.end`; `next()` returns `\0` and moves `pos` to `end + 1`, and `backup()` immediately decrements to `end` and dereferences `*lexer->pos`. The saved ASan trace reports that one-byte out-of-bounds read at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:279` in `backup`. The staged fix changes the fuzz-only helper to call `config_init_data(config, data, len - 1)`, leaving one in-bounds byte of slack for that lookahead/backup sequence.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the copied fuzz buffer and its clipped length: the fuzz-only helper starts config parsing on exactly `len` bytes from `data`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 32770 bytes. In `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc`, the harness clamps `size` to `sizeof(static_data) = 32768`, copies that prefix into `static_data`, and then calls this helper with `data = static_data` and `len = 32768`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `backup()` dereferences `lexer->pos` after decrementing from the EOF-lookahead state, and on the witnessed path that pointer equals `static_data + 32768`, one byte past the global buffer.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Lexer initialization derives `lexer.end` from the full clipped fuzz length, so for this witness `lexer.end` becomes `static_data + 32768`, the first byte past the copied array. The later EOF lookahead in `peek()` steps back to and inspects that boundary. The staged fix avoids this state by having `config_open_for_fuzzing()` pass `len - 1`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled state is the clipped buffer length `len`. On the witnessed path it is 32768, and `config_init_data()` later turns that full length into the out-of-bounds boundary pointer `lexer.end`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The harness truncates the 32770-byte staged `poc` to the first 32768 bytes before entering this project helper.

parser_admitted.description: After truncating and copying the fuzz input into `static_data`, the harness dispatches that buffer into the project's config parser via `config_open_for_fuzzing()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness truncates the 32770-byte witness to 32768 bytes, fills `static_data` with that prefix, and then hands the full array-length buffer to `config_open_for_fuzzing()`.

The fuzz-only helper initializes the lexer on the full clipped buffer, and `config_init_data()` derives `lexer.end = data + len`, which makes the EOF boundary equal to the first byte past `static_data`.

When `lex_config()` reads the copied tail byte `$`, it evaluates the `$` lookahead at EOF; `next()` moves `lexer->pos` to `lexer.end + 1`, and `backup()` immediately decrements and dereferences `*lexer->pos` at `lexer.end`, causing the observed one-byte global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The staged `poc` is 32770 bytes, so the harness clips it to `size = 32768` and copies only that prefix into the global `static_data[32768]`. The copied prefix fills the array completely, and its last copied byte is `0x24` (`'$'`).

Source. The fuzz-only project helper consumes the copied buffer and its clipped length and initializes config parsing on exactly `len` bytes. On the witnessed run that means the parser is started on the full 32768-byte `static_data` capacity, with no byte held back for lookahead slack.

Root cause. Using the full clipped length makes `lexer.end` equal to `static_data + 32768`, the first byte past the copied global buffer. Later EOF lookahead uses this boundary as the place to step back to.

When the lexer reaches the final in-bounds byte of the copied prefix, `next()` returns `0x24` (`'$'`) into `chr` and advances `lexer->pos` to `lexer.end`. This is the last attacker-controlled character consumed before the overflow.
Because the last consumed byte is `$`, the short-circuit condition evaluates `peek(lexer)` even though `lexer->pos` already equals `lexer.end`. That control decision enters the EOF lookahead path.

Inside `peek`, the EOF guard sees there is no byte left after the final `$`, so it returns `\0` and moves `lexer->pos` to `lexer->end + 1` without reading another input byte. That leaves `backup()` one decrement away from the out-of-bounds boundary from step 3.

Sink. `backup()` decrements `lexer->pos` from `lexer->end + 1` to `lexer->end` and immediately dereferences `*lexer->pos`. Since `lexer->end` is `static_data + 32768`, that read lands exactly one byte past the global `static_data` array, matching the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow` READ 1 at line 279.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the saved ASan crash location `backup` at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:279`, which is frame 0 in both staged crash traces.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `backup -> peek -> lex_config -> lex_next -> parse_config -> parser_next -> config_read_line` matches the fine trace's lookahead and parser steps and the surrounding coarse trace.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The clipped full-buffer length becomes `lexer.end`, the copied tail byte `$` triggers `peek()` at EOF, and `backup()` then dereferences the resulting boundary pointer at the sink.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_18464 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` READ 1 in `backup`.

format.name: raw config-fuzzer byte stream
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 32770-byte blob in `gt_results/arvo_18464/poc`. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to the witnessed truncation and tail layout: the harness copies only the first 32768 bytes into `static_data[32768]`, that copied prefix fills the array completely, and its final copied byte is `0x24` (`'$'`). In `lex_config()`, the lexer reads that final `$` as the last in-bounds character and immediately executes the `$` lookahead `peek(lexer)` at EOF; `backup()` then reads one byte past `static_data`. The saved artifacts do not justify a broader input class beyond this exact clipped layout.
